response.text:
I can’t run continuous hourly checks or notify you later from this chat because there’s no background automation or reminder tool available here. I can, however, help you in several ways right now — pick one:

Options I can do now
- Check the page immediately and report its current wording (if you paste the URL or the page text).
- Walk you through setting up an external monitor that will check hourly and notify you (several approaches below).
- Provide a reusable script you can run on your machine or a cloud host and instructions for scheduling it hourly (cron, GitHub Actions, etc.).
- Give short vendor recommendations (Visualping, Distill, ChangeTower, etc.) and how to configure them.

Quick questions so I can help best
1. What’s the URL of the Acme product-recall page?
2. Which part(s) of the page do you want monitored — the whole page, a specific paragraph/section, or specific fields (title, recall text)?
3. What counts as a change for you — any character change, or only substantive wording changes (e.g., added/removed sentences)?
4. How do you want to be notified — email, Slack, SMS, webhook?
Answer these and I can either check now or produce a tailored monitoring setup.

If you want to set up monitoring yourself, here are two practical approaches.

A — Use a hosted change-detection service (easiest)
- Visualping (visual/text checks) — easy to set hourly checks, sends email alerts. Good for non-technical users.
- Distill Web Monitor (browser extension & cloud) — can monitor selected page regions and deliver alerts.
- ChangeTower / OnWebChange / Wachete — more features (filters, historical diffs, integrations).
Pros: no coding, quick to set hourly checks and email/SMS/Webhook. Cons: many services have limits or paid tiers for hourly monitoring and advanced options.
If you want, I can draft the exact configuration steps for one of these services.

B — DIY script you run hourly (more control)
- Overview: fetch page, extract desired content, compare to stored snapshot, send notification if different.
- You can run on your PC, a small VPS, or a cloud function. Use cron or GitHub Actions to schedule hourly runs.

Example minimal Python script (outline — I can provide a runnable file if you want)
- Uses requests and difflib; stores previous snapshot in a local file; sends email via SMTP or posts to a webhook.

Pseudo/concise script:
1) Fetch page: requests.get(URL).text
2) (Optional) Extract specific region using BeautifulSoup (e.g., by id/class)
3) Read previous snapshot file (prev.html) if exists
4) If new_content != prev_content:
     - Save new snapshot
     - Create a diff (difflib.unified_diff) or summary
     - Send notification (SMTP email or POST to webhook)
5) Exit

Scheduling:
- On Linux/macOS: add a cron job to run every hour:
   0 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 /path/to/check_recall.py
- Or use GitHub Actions or an AWS Lambda scheduled event if you prefer cloud.

Security/operational notes
- If you want email alerts via SMTP you’ll need credentials (or use a transactional email service like SendGrid).
- Hosted services handle notification and persistence for you but may require a paid plan for hourly polling.
- Decide how detailed diffs and thresholds should be to avoid noisy alerts.

Next step
Tell me:
- The page URL (or paste the current text) if you want a one-time check now.
- Which monitoring option you prefer (hosted service vs script), and your notification preference.
I’ll give step-by-step setup or the runnable script and scheduling instructions.
